headline_marked: 60% of e-return filers [[show no taxable income]], says former finance adviser
headline: 60% of e-return filers show no taxable income, says former finance adviser
summary: Former finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed reveals a surprising lack of taxable income among e-return filers, attributing poor tax collection to public reluctance and NBR resistance to digitisation.
details: Former finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed stated that approximately 60 percent of people who filed e-returns reported no taxable income during his tenure under the interim government.
He expressed surprise at the figure, noting that even rickshaw pullers often earn more than the tax-free ceiling of Tk 3,50,000.
Ahmed identified a general reluctance to pay taxes as a primary cause for the National Board of Revenue's (NBR) poor tax collection performance.
He further claimed that resistance to automation and digitisation within the NBR is driven by the desire of officials to take bribes, which digital systems would prevent.
Regarding money laundering, he mentioned that 11 sensitive cases have been identified, with recovery of funds possible within three to four years.
He also revealed that the Adani conglomerate nearly halted electricity supplies to Bangladesh, but continued after the finance ministry paid Tk 100 crore via the energy ministry.
On the budget for FY27, he cautioned that the NBR's revenue target of Tk 700,000 crore is overly ambitious given current capacity and tax structure constraints.
While welcoming the prioritised allocation for social sectors like health and education, he stressed that the government must ensure monitoring capacity to ensure the actual expenditure.
caption:
60% of e-return filers report zero taxable income. Why is Bangladesh's tax collection so poor?

Former finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed stated that approximately 60 percent of people who filed e-returns reported no taxable income during his tenure under the interim government.

He expressed surprise at the figure, noting that even rickshaw pullers often earn more than the tax-free ceiling of Tk 3,50,000.

Ahmed identified a general reluctance to pay taxes as a primary cause for the National Board of Revenue's (NBR) poor tax collection performance.

He further claimed that resistance to automation and digitisation within the NBR is driven by the desire of officials to take bribes, which digital systems would prevent.

Regarding money laundering, he mentioned that 11 sensitive cases have been identified, with recovery of funds possible within three to four years.

He also revealed that the Adani conglomerate nearly halted electricity supplies to Bangladesh, but continued after the finance ministry paid Tk 100 crore via the energy ministry.

On the budget for FY27, he cautioned that the NBR's revenue target of Tk 700,000 crore is overly ambitious given current capacity and tax structure constraints.

While welcoming the prioritised allocation for social sectors like health and education, he stressed that the government must ensure monitoring capacity to ensure the actual expenditure.

headline: Bogura: Madrasa teacher beaten after attempting to rape child student
summary: A teacher was lynched by a mob in Bogura following allegations of an attempted sexual assault on a young student.
details: A madrasa teacher in Bogura was subjected to a public beating by a mob after he allegedly attempted to rape a child student.
The incident sparked immediate outrage among local residents, who gathered and attacked the accused teacher upon learning of the alleged crime.
Police intervened to rescue the accused from the mob and have taken him into custody for further investigation.
Local authorities are currently looking into the details of the assault and the circumstances surrounding the attempted rape of the minor student.
